title: Solar Rebates in Cambridge 2026: Up to $10,000 and a RetrofitWR Loan
desc: Cambridge solar rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings, with GrandBridge Energy as the utility and a local loan of up to $40,000 at 2.5%.
lead: Cambridge pairs the provincial solar rebate with RetrofitWR, a loan of up to $40,000 at 2.5% fixed for GrandBridge Energy customers. Confirm whether solar fits the loan's 25% energy-saving test.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for solar and batteries in Cambridge
cards_intro: We re-read the program's solar page and its October 2025 requirements on October 3, 2026. The rebate comes with conditions that change how the system is designed, so read them before you ask for quotes.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: Paid on installed DC capacity, capped at 50% of eligible costs. Rooftop systems only, including a garage roof on the same meter.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Only with a new solar system, also capped at 50% of eligible costs. Combined solar and battery rebates reach $10,000.

cards.title: No net metering
cards.amount: Rebate excluded if you net meter
cards.note: A system under an Ontario net metering agreement is not eligible. The system must be sized for load displacement only.

cards.title: Approvals before you buy
cards.note: The contractor files the pre-installation application with a quote dated within 60 days. You cannot buy or install before IESO pre-approval and your local utility's approval.

cards.title: Finish within 12 months
cards.note: The project must be complete within 12 months of approval, with the ESA certificate and the connection agreement filed within 30 days of installation.

cards.title: First-time installs only
cards.note: Homes that already have solar or storage are not eligible. Leases, rentals and lease-to-own arrangements are excluded.

cards.title: RetrofitWR loan
cards.note: Up to $40,000 over 10 or 15 years. For GrandBridge Energy customers in Cambridge and North Dumfries, repaid on the bill, for projects that cut energy use by 25% or more.

after_cards: The requirements document gives no end date for this stream, and funding conditions can change, so confirm on the program page before you sign. The IESO has no pre-qualified contractor list for it.
sections: GrandBridge Energy is the distribution company. It approves the connection and also repays the RetrofitWR loan on its bill, for customers in Cambridge and North Dumfries. The loan needs a project that cuts energy use by at least 25%, so ask the Region how solar generation counts.
77% of Cambridge households live in an eligible house type and 69% own. Peak sun is about 3.9 hours a day, and 5.2% report needing major repairs.
The Region's Energy Coach is free to homeowners across Waterloo Region and can help you plan.

Many Ontario solar quotes assume net metering, where extra power sent to the grid earns bill credits. This program does not allow it: a system under a net metering agreement is not eligible, and the system must be sized for load displacement, meaning it should match what the home uses. A Cambridge owner who wants the rebate should tell every installer up front, because a system designed to export will not qualify.

The panels must be on the roof of the house or of a permanent structure on the same property and connected to the home's meter, such as a detached garage. Ground mounts are not eligible, and neither are systems on trailers or other temporary structures. Cambridge has 29,105 detached houses, where roof orientation and shading decide the system size.

The rebate is capped at 50% of eligible costs, which cover equipment, permits, approvals and labour. HST, financing costs, insurance, maintenance and spare parts are not eligible costs. A quote should therefore show the pre-HST price and separate any financing, so the program can check that $1,000 per kW does not exceed half.

The order matters. The contractor submits the pre-installation application with a quote dated within 60 days, you receive written pre-approval and your utility's approval, and only then do you buy and install. The system must be finished within 12 months of approval, and the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days of installation.
claim_steps: Confirm you own an eligible house type with a roof or garage that suits panels.
Talk to GrandBridge Energy about the connection process and the maximum system size allowed before you sign anything.
Choose a licensed electrical contractor and ask for a quote that shows the DC capacity in kW and the eligible costs without HST.
Let the contractor file the pre-installation application, and wait for written IESO pre-approval and utility approval before buying or installing.
After the install, check that the post-installation application is filed within 30 days with the ESA certificate and connection agreement.
